reviewer.name: Codex independent source reviewer /root/date_slice, incorporating earlier /root/disk_audit findings

summary: Partial independent source review, preserving existing King Wu, Bi Gan and Xinling findings and adding dream, kinship and historical-allusion date ownership concerns. Not a complete chapter audit or approval.

itemChecks.event: King Wu acts at Bi Gan's tomb; Sui later recalls that action.
itemChecks.reason: The source does not state an absolute year, and the reconstructed text 武王比干 is not contiguous in the Chinese. The claim represents BC 1046 as year precision without an identified supporting conversion or uncertainty.

itemChecks.event: Bi Gan is recalled as the honoree of an action at his tomb.
itemChecks.reason: The cited unit gives no exact Western year, and the tomb action is not evidence that Bi Gan was personally active then. Its sourceDate wording is not contiguous in the cited Chinese.

itemChecks.event: King Wu's active-date hint for the historical tomb action.
itemChecks.reason: BC 1046 is not stated by this source and competing scholarly chronologies differ; assess independently whether and how external evidence supports any narrower activity hint.

itemChecks.event: Bi Gan's historical active-date hint, separate from later tomb commemoration.
itemChecks.reason: BC 1100 is not given in this source and this reviewer has not identified a source establishing it as Bi Gan's activity year.

itemChecks.event: Han Gaozu sacrifices at Lord Xinling's grave; Sui later recalls the sacrifice.
itemChecks.reason: The cited sentence is a tomb sacrifice, not an attestation of Xinling's living activity during Gaozu's BC 206–195 reign; its sourceDate text is not contiguous and the sentence does not specify those Western endpoints.

itemChecks.event: Lord Xinling's active-date hint, distinct from Han Gaozu's later sacrifice.
itemChecks.reason: The staged hint BC 275-243 is not stated in this unit; its independent source, meaning and endpoints require research rather than automatic deletion or approval.

itemChecks.event: Chui compares Murong De to the earlier figure Lü Meng.
itemChecks.reason: This comparison is a later reference to Lü Meng, not a living attestation dated to AD 200–219. The quoted comparison itself gives no Western endpoints; a distinct source is needed to support any personal activity date.

itemChecks.event: De recalls Wu Chen advising King Zhuang of Chu.
itemChecks.reason: This source is a later speaker’s retrospective example and does not establish a living attestation in BC 584. The quoted passage supplies no absolute year; research the historical event separately.

itemChecks.event: De recalls King Zhuang of Chu setting aside Xia Ji.
itemChecks.reason: This source is a later speaker’s retrospective example and does not establish Xia Ji’s living attestation in BC 584. The passage itself supplies no absolute year; research the underlying event separately.

itemChecks.event: Murong Chao arrives after his uncle summoned him from Chang’an.
itemChecks.reason: Calling Chao the son of De’s brother identifies a familial relationship but does not attest that Chao’s father was alive or personally active in AD 403–405.

itemChecks.event: Murong De dreams that his father speaks to him.
itemChecks.reason: The cited dream represents the father as speaking in De’s dream; it is not a living attestation during AD 337–348, and neither endpoint is supplied by this unit.

personChecks.reason: This local record has one source-dated claim; the cited unit provides no absolute year and its conversion needs independently reviewed evidence.
The cited unit concerns Bi Gan's tomb and cannot on its own establish a date of personal activity; the additional BC 1100 hint needs research.
The tomb reference cannot support a living attestation during Gaozu's reign, and the separate active-date hint needs its own independent sourcing.

findings.problem: The cited text does not supply the precise 1046 BC year attached to King Wu's tomb action or establish the disconnected sourceDate wording.
findings.action: Reconcile the undated action and activity hint using a source-backed repair, preserve any genuine uncertainty, and obtain a fresh independent audit of the exact repaired extraction.

findings.problem: A tomb commemoration is presented as a dated personal attestation and the additional BC 1100 hint lacks evidence in this review.
findings.action: Separate the retrospective tomb reference from living activity, research the activity hint rather than guessing, and independently audit the resulting exact source and extraction.

findings.problem: The later grave sacrifice is recorded as Xinling's dated personal attestation; the independent basis of his separate active-date hint is not established in this review.
findings.action: Retain the historical sacrifice as an independently reviewed retrospective reference, correct the living-attestation ownership, research the existing hint, and fully re-audit exact repaired bytes.

findings.problem: A later literary comparison is used to date Lü Meng’s personal activity to AD 200–219 without a supporting source for either endpoint.
findings.action: Preserve the later comparison as an appropriately evidenced retrospective reference, research any independent living activity dates, and obtain a fresh independent audit.

findings.problem: Two people recalled in a later quotation are given exact BC 584 living attestations even though the quotation supplies no such date.
findings.action: Preserve each recalled historical example separately from living activity, research the source and dating of the historical episode, and independently review the corrected extraction.

findings.problem: Chao’s familial relationship to his uncle is misused to date the personal activity of Chao’s father to AD 403–405.
findings.action: Correct the ownership of the attestation without deleting the independently evidenced relationship; research the separate date hint and obtain a fresh independent audit.

findings.problem: A deceased father’s dream appearance is encoded as a living attestation in AD 337–348 without endpoint support in the cited text.
findings.action: Preserve the dream reference as later reception where appropriate and research the father’s actual activity independently; reconcile the separate duplicate identity before publication.

references.title: Pengcheng Zhang, The Chronology of Western Zhou
references.reason: The article discusses three candidate conquest years, supporting the need to research competing chronologies rather than treat one year as certain in this undated local text.

references.title: Shiji 77: Biography of Lord Xinling
references.reason: The biography places Gaozu's sacrifice after Xinling's death and tomb establishment; it supports identifying the grave-side event as retrospective, not living activity.
